verdict.probe_answer: Test files are byte-identical between arms, so rigor is equal. All 7 added tests assert real behavior (confidence/kind/resolved-file/pool-size), not trivial checks, and most flip RED→GREEN vs pre-Task-5 code per the plan's own log (inherent+trait demote, unresolved-owner keep-all, both ①C shadow tests, the Pending-alias test). Strongest in each: scope_graph_pending_import_alias_over_colliding_pool_keeps_all — it pins a colliding pool AND explicitly discriminates the correct call-site-rib directness oracle from a plausible-but-wrong global-search oracle that would silently over-prune and drop a real edge. Weakest in each: scope_graph_two_crate_owner_collision_recovers_to_single_exact — per the plan's own RED notes this already passes pre-Task-5 (Task 4's graph_target_resolution alone yields 1→Exact here), so it's more an end-to-end regression pin than a discriminator of Task 5's new wiring. Both arms also share a gap: neither added the brief's required 'mixed-edition keep-all' test (present in ground truth as scope_graph_non_uniform_edition_keeps_all), so the edition_uniform guard has no Task-5-level regression pin in either diff.
verdict.rationale: Arm B matches the real ground-truth Task-5 commit (63c52c5) on the actual branch almost verbatim: same helper placement, same prune/fail-open logic, same tests. Arm A inserts an extra unrequested gate before the fail-open (drop when a separate qualified-edge query resolves to an empty id-set) that isn't in the plan's Step-3 code, is untested by either arm's identical test suite, and doesn't match how the project's real later trait-CHA regression was actually fixed (a follow-up commit checked ResolutionKind::TraitCha, not id-set emptiness). That's unauthorized scope creep on a task demanding 'exactly as specified' + 'STOP and report' on mismatch, risking a coincidental recall drop the spec exists to prevent. Both arms omit the brief's required 'mixed-edition keep-all' test equally.
